papers.title: How far is Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness from Martin-L\"of randomness?
papers.abstract: We'll call a map from basic to clopen sets of binary sequences an \textit{encoding} if it preserves uniform Lebesgue measure and the disjointedness relation. For some notion of randomness $R$ we can ask if there is a computable encoding $E$ such that for every non-Martin-L\"of-random (non-MLR) sequence $\alpha$, the sequences in $E(\alpha)$ are non-$R$. Thus we can use $E$ and randomness test for $R$ to construct a randomness test for MLR. We show that there is no such $E$ for partial computable randomness (PCR), but there is one for Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness. Indeed, there is a total computable $E$ and a pair of total computable non-monotonic betting strategies such that on every sequence in $E(\alpha)$ at least one of the strategies wins whenever $\alpha$ is non-MLR.

papers.title: On the hardness of approximating minimum distances of quantum codes
papers.abstract: The problem of computing distances of error-correcting codes is fundamental in both the classical and quantum settings. While hardness for the classical version of these problems has been known for some time (in both the exact and approximate settings), it was only recently that Kapshikar and Kundu showed these problems are also hard in the quantum setting. As our first main result, we reprove this using arguably simpler arguments based on hypergraph product codes. In particular, we get a direct reduction to CSS codes, the most commonly used type of quantum code, from the minimum distance problem for classical linear codes. Our second set of results considers the distance of a graph state, which is a key parameter for quantum codes obtained via the codeword stabilized formalism. We show that it is NP-hard to compute/approximate the distance of a graph state when the adjacency matrix of the graph is the input. In fact, we show this is true even if we only consider X-type errors of a graph state. Our techniques moreover imply an interesting classical consequence: the hardness of computing or approximating the distance of classical codes with rate equal to 1/2. One of the main motivations of the present work is a question raised by Kapshikar and Kundu concerning the NP-hardness of approximation when there is an additive error proportional to a quantum code's length. We show that no such hardness can hold for hypergraph product codes. These observations suggest the possibility of a new kind of square root barrier.

papers.title: Conditional Vendi Score: Prompt-Aware Diversity Evaluation for Generative AI Models and LLMs
papers.abstract: Generative models guided by text prompts are widely evaluated for fidelity and prompt alignment, yet their ability to produce diverse outputs remains underexplored. Existing diversity metrics such as Vendi and RKE, which are based on the von Neumann and R\'enyi entropies of kernel matrices, were developed for unconditional models and cannot distinguish prompt-induced from model-induced variability. We address this gap by introducing \textit{Conditional-Vendi} and \textit{Conditional-RKE}, diversity measures derived from the conditional entropy of positive semidefinite matrices. These scores isolate model-induced diversity in prompt-guided generation, with Conditional-RKE enjoying an $O(1/\sqrt{n})$ convergence rate. For Conditional-Vendi, we introduce a truncated-spectrum approximation that yields scalable and consistent estimates. Experiments on text-to-image, image-captioning, and LLM tasks show that the conditional scores recover ground-truth diversity orderings and can also guide diffusion models toward more diverse samples. The codebase is available at https://github.com/mjalali/conditional-vendi.

papers.title: Towards a Measure Theory of Semantic Information
papers.abstract: A classic account of the quantification of semantic information is that of Bar-Hiller and Carnap. Their account proposes an inverse relation between the informativeness of a statement and its probability. However, their approach assigns the maximum informativeness to a contradiction: which Floridi refers to as the Bar-Hillel-Carnap paradox. He developed a novel theory founded on a distance metric and parabolic relation, designed to remove this paradox. Unfortunately is approach does not succeed in that aim. In this paper I critique Floridi's theory of strongly semantic information on its own terms and show where it succeeds and fails. I then present a new approach based on the unit circle (a relation that has been the basis of theories from basic trigonometry to quantum theory). This is used, by analogy with von Neumann's quantum probability to construct a measure space for informativeness that meets all the requirements stipulated by Floridi and removes the paradox. In addition, while contradictions and tautologies have zero informativeness, it is found that messages which are contradictory to each other are equally informative. The utility of this is explained by means of an example.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Masked Diffusion Models Provably Learn Distributions with Latent Structure
papers.abstract: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) generate discrete data by iteratively unmasking multiple tokens in parallel using a learned mask predictor. Their output carries two errors: parallelization error due to parallel sampling, and estimation error from the mask predictor learned with finite samples. Existing theory treats these errors separately, and the available statistical bounds typically scale with the number $V^L$ of length-$L$ sequences over a vocabulary of size $V$, suffering from the curse of dimensionality. In this work, we establish end-to-end statistical guarantees showing that transformer-based MDMs learn structured distributions with a sample complexity governed by their latent structure. Specifically, we model this structure through mixtures of hidden Markov trees, which capture latent dependencies within components and heterogeneity across components. When the data distribution is well approximated by such a mixture, a transformer-based MDM with parallel unmasking schedules achieves $\varepsilon$-accurate sampling in KL divergence with $\widetilde{O}(LK_{\mathrm{par}}/\varepsilon)$ training samples, where $K_{\mathrm{par}}$ is polynomial in $L$, $V$, the number of hidden states, and the number of mixture components. The transformer network and sampling procedure require no knowledge of the tree topologies or component parameters, thereby adapting to the unknown latent structure automatically. Overall, our results provide theoretical justification for the empirical effectiveness of MDMs on real-world data.

papers.title: Low-Complexity SVD-Based Precoding over Zero-Padded ISI Channels
papers.abstract: We propose a low-complexity SVD-based transceiver for zero-padded memory-$1$ ISI channels. Appending a single zero-padding symbol to an $n$-symbol block yields an $n\times(n-1)$ channel matrix with an \emph{exact symmetric tridiagonal Toeplitz Gram matrix}. This structure provides closed-form singular values and vectors, enabling exact SVD precoding and equalization via FFTs without explicitly forming dense SVD matrices. The resulting implementation has $O(n\log n)$ complexity and incurs only a $1/n$ rate penalty. The resulting parallel scalar subchannels enable joint adaptive PAM and power allocation for SER minimization, followed by exact soft-information computation for LDPC decoding. At comparable code rates near $0.945$, simulations show that our proposed scheme outperforms a conventional TX-FFE/RX-DFE system with hard-decision Reed-Solomon (RS) decoding by approximately $5$ dB at FER $10^{-5}$. At high SNR, it achieves nearly the same FER performance as a SOVA-based receiver with LDPC decoding, while replacing trellis-based detection with fast SVD precoding and exact scalar soft-output computation.

papers.title: DataCupid: Stable Matching Repair for Training Data Acquisition with Delayed Feedback
papers.abstract: Matching repair after utility changes can reuse valid observations, but new evaluations must respect matching capacity and may return out of order. We study announced invalidations with bounded, possibly reward-dependent reporting delays and pending evaluations that do not occupy future matching capacity. Residualload repair (RLR) combines sound outcome certificates with batched matching schedules for unequal sample deficits. Its complete dyadic quota schedule admits a sharp issue-round bound with coefficient cb < 1.607 relative to the terminal residual endpoint load, together with separate delay and evidence-lifetime bounds. RLR-P monitors complete issue-order prefixes without changing the sampling plan before acceptance. With a deterministic pure oracle, a single-repair coupling from the same drained initial state guarantees no increase in certification time, issued observations, or time to a reusable checkpoint. We also derive an information-load lower bound. On fixed priority-star markets with unknown Bernoulli gaps, PrioritySearch attains the history-adjusted first-order constant for expected certification time as {\delta} {\sim} 0, under hypothesis-independent linear history scaling and sublogarithmic reporting delays. Paired simulations and measured-feedback replay quantify the trade-offs: in the replay, RLR-P has lower mean capped update-certification time than a monitored width-based baseline, at higher oracle CPU cost.

papers.title: Beyond Hypercontractivity: Stronger Communication Converses via R\'enyi Contraction
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between strong data-processing inequalities for R\'enyi divergences and hypercontractivity. For R\'enyi divergences of order greater than one, we characterize the contraction of R\'enyi divergences through a property of the dual Markov operator that we name power contraction. Using the contraction coefficient, we derive an upper bound on rectangle probabilities in terms of their marginals that is at least as strong as the corresponding bound obtained via hypercontractivity. Combining this result with inversion of the binary R\'enyi divergence, we derive communication lower bounds for one-way communication-assisted agreement distillation. Examples involving binary symmetric and rare-event Z-channels illustrate the improvements over standard hypercontractive converses.

papers.title: A Ray-Traced Digital Twin for 5G NR Positioning with OpenAirInterface
papers.abstract: Evaluating 5G positioning on a physical testbed ties every measurement to one propagation environment and one antenna layout, so any question about an alternative deployment requires a new field campaign. We present a ray-traced digital twin of the GEO-5G testbed at EURECOM that drives an unmodified OpenAirInterface (OAI) 5G stack with per-antenna channels computed by Sionna-RT over a 3D model of the site. The distributed gNB antennas are modelled as independent radio devices rather than as elements of a compact array, which preserves the per-antenna absolute delays on which time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) positioning depends. With them preserved, the twin drives OAI's SRS-based UL-TDoA pipeline to metre-level accuracy consistent with that reported for the physical deployment. We then use the twin to answer a question the physical testbed cannot. Widening the carrier truncates the tail of the horizontal error distribution without improving a typical position, and leaves the vertical error untouched, because the latter is limited by the array geometry rather than by the measurement. That limit is predictable from the antenna coordinates alone, and a height-diverse layout reduces the RMS height error by a factor of four.

papers.title: Structure-Aware Online Optimization of the Age of Information with Unknown System Statistics
papers.abstract: Timely information dissemination is essential in modern communication systems, where low informational latency is critical for networked control, monitoring, and real-time decision-making. The Age of Information (AoI) has emerged as a fundamental metric for quantifying information freshness at the receiver. A key challenge in AoI optimization is selecting the update generation rate: infrequent updates lead to stale information, whereas overly frequent updates increase queueing delays. We develop a structure-aware, data-driven framework for adaptive AoI optimization modeled as single-server queues with unknown system statistics. Our key idea is to exploit analytical representations of the AoI gradient, which depend on a finite-dimensional collection of system quantities that can be estimated from observations collected during system operation. This reduces the online learning problem to estimating the quantities required by the gradient, rather than learning the AoI objective as a black box. We propose an online stochastic approximation algorithm that jointly estimates these quantities and optimizes the update generation rate. We prove almost sure convergence of the algorithm to the optimal update generation rate under mild regularity and moment conditions, despite the temporal dependence induced by the underlying queueing process. We demonstrate the framework in four representative incomplete-information settings, including FCFS queues with unknown service characteristics or hidden background traffic, a preemptive LCFS system with partial observations, and a generate-at-will system with threshold waiting.

papers.title: Goal-Oriented Ordered Autoencoding for Successive Refinement in Progressive Communication
papers.abstract: Goal-oriented communication often struggles to sustain downstream task performance under variable and unpredictable bandwidth. We address this problem by proposing GO-OAE (Goal-Oriented Ordered AutoEncoding), which learns a progressively refinable quantized latent sequence, optimized directly for task utility rather than source reconstruction. Each component of the sequence is represented for transmission by its code index, and the learned ordering enables inference from any received prefix of the index sequence, with performance improving as more indices arrive. We prove that optimizing the goal-oriented distortion objective is equivalent to solving a weighted conditional information bottleneck formulation, and introduce an unbiased multi-prefix importance sampling (MPIS) estimator, to reduce GO-OAE training computational cost from O(BK) to O(Bm) with m << K, and reduces the estimator variance by a factor of 1/m. Experiments show that, on MiniImageNet, GO-OAE achieves over 96% of the lossless upper-bound classification accuracy using 324 bits per image (683X compression vs. raw RGB), and already attains over 94% of the upper bound with only 70% of the transmitted indices. It consistently outperforms reconstruction-optimized codecs and ordered autoencoders trained with uniform prefix sampling across all transmission budgets, demonstrating effective communication at extreme compression rates.

papers.title: Gaussian BROJA Partial Information Decomposition in Closed Form
papers.abstract: The BROJA partial information decomposition provides an operationally motivated way to separate the information that two sources carry about a target into unique, redundant, and synergistic components. For continuous and high-dimensional variables, however, computing the BROJA decomposition requires solving a difficult optimization problem. Previous work showed that, when each source-target pair is jointly Gaussian, the problem can be reduced to finite-dimensional numerical optimization. Here, we derive a closed-form solution to this optimization problem, enabling direct computation of the BROJA decomposition in the general multivariate Gaussian setting. The resulting closed-form expression enables speedups exceeding two orders of magnitude for high-dimensional Gaussian BROJA PID. Code is available at https://github.com/brainsandmachines/Eigen_PID.

papers.title: Neural Polar Codes for Source Coding
papers.abstract: This paper presents a data-driven approach to lossless and lossy source compression using polar codes. Classical polar source coding achieves fundamental limits with low complexity for binary memoryless sources. However, for unknown q-ary sources with memory, successive-cancellation (SC) decoding requires an explicit source model and can be computationally prohibitive. We present analytical SC recursions and show that exact implementations scale quadratically with alphabet size and cubically with state-space size. To overcome these limitations, we develop neural polar decoders trained directly from data to approximate conditional distributions of synthetic polar coordinates without requiring an explicit source model. These learned distributions enable estimation of entropy rates, mutual information, and rate-distortion functions, and support explicit polar compression schemes. For lossless compression, we identify high-entropy polarized coordinates and reconstruct the remaining coordinates using the learned SC recursion. For lossy compression, we combine neural polar decoders with a neural test channel to estimate and optimize the mutual information-distortion tradeoff and construct an explicit lossy polar code. We also extend the framework to Wyner-Ziv compression with decoder side information by learning conditional polarized distributions and a reconstruction mapping. Experiments on memoryless sources, sources with memory, and real genomic data show that the learned decoders closely match analytical SC decoders when available and remain applicable when conventional methods are computationally infeasible or the source model is unavailable.

papers.title: On Privacy Mechanism Design Under a Bounded $\alpha$-Lift Leakage Constraint with $\chi^2$-Utility
papers.abstract: We study the design of a statistical privacy mechanism under a bounded $\alpha$-lift leakage constraint. An agent observes useful data $Y$, which is arbitrarily correlated with private data $X$, and releases $U$. The goal is to maximize Pearson $\chi^2$-information $\chi^2(Y;U)$ while satisfying the point-wise privacy constraint. This utility is an $f$-information that is nonnegative, obeys data processing, and measures the aggregate normalized change from the prior $P_Y$ to the posteriors $P_{Y|U=u}$. The main benefit of this choice is that $\chi^2(Y;U)$ is exactly quadratic in the posterior perturbations; hence, no local approximation of the utility is required. For the nonlinear $\alpha$-lift constraint, we derive a uniform Taylor-remainder bound that remains valid for the optimizing, $\epsilon$-dependent perturbation. When $P_{X|Y}$ is invertible, this yields a closed-form quadratic surrogate, an explicitly scaled binary mechanism that satisfies the original $\alpha$-lift constraint, a computable sufficient range for $\epsilon$, and an $O(\epsilon^{3/2})$ bound on the utility gap. For $\alpha=2$, the solution is exact over an explicit range. We transfer these results to point-wise R\'enyi-divergence privacy, including an exact-feasible mechanism, an explicit privacy-budget range, and matching gap bounds. We also give an exact formulation for arbitrary leakage matrices and evaluate exact-feasible mechanisms numerically.

papers.title: Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations
papers.abstract: Consider a queueing system operated by Bob, which is intended to serve only jobs generated by a legitimate user, Willie. Willie's jobs arrive according to a Poisson process, and the service times are exponentially distributed. Bob seeks to covertly serve additional jobs arriving according to an independent Poisson process, without Willie detecting their presence. As the legitimate user, Willie is provided with certain statistics of each busy period by Bob. In particular, we consider two statistics: (i) the number of jobs served during each busy period and (ii) the duration of each busy period. We establish that, under either statistic, the maximum expected number of additional jobs that Bob can covertly serve obeys a square-root law. Specifically, over n busy periods, Bob can covertly serve additional jobs in the order of square root of n, whereas any scaling which is above square root of n enables Willie to asymptotically detect the presence of these additional jobs with vanishing error probability. Furthermore, we characterize the scaling constant associated with the square-root law, which we refer to as the covert queueing constant, for each of the two statistics. We compare the scaling constants corresponding to the two statistics and argue that the scaling constant under statistic (i) is no greater than that under statistic (ii).

papers.title: Heterogeneous Demand-Private Coded Caching: Exact Characterization for Two Users and Two Files
papers.abstract: We consider the demand-private coded caching problem with heterogeneous file sizes and cache capacities, where each user must recover its requested file without learning any information about the demands of the other users. We first extend the virtual-user reduction technique to accommodate heterogeneous cache sizes, thereby enabling the construction of demand-private coded caching schemes from non-private schemes. Our main contribution is an exact characterization of the memory-rate trade-off for the fundamental setting of two users and two files with arbitrary file sizes and cache capacities. Specifically, we characterize the optimal trade-off through eight linear inequalities and establish achievability by constructing explicit coded caching schemes for the non-trivial corner points, followed by memory sharing. These constructions include novel asymmetric cache placement strategies tailored to heterogeneous file sizes and cache capacities. For the converse, we exploit the distributional equivalences induced by demand privacy to derive information-theoretic lower bounds that explicitly account for the underlying heterogeneity. Our results generalize the exact memory-rate trade-off characterization for the homogeneous demand-private coded caching setting with two users and two files, while quantifying the additional transmission cost imposed by demand privacy compared with the non-private heterogeneous setting.

papers.title: KL Before and After Mixing: A Round-Complexity Separation in Parallel Sampling
papers.abstract: A parallel sampler can choose at random which coordinates to generate together. For a target $p$ and the output law $q_U$ of a schedule $U$ drawn afresh for each output, we compare the schedule-averaged divergence $\mathbb{E}_U D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q_U)$ with the output-law divergence $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|\mathbb{E}_U q_U)$, in nats. Rounds commit independent draws from exact conditional marginals frozen at the round's start, each output's schedule is drawn before sampling from a finite mixture of schedules, and every scheduled round is charged. For the uniform distribution on binary strings of even length $n$ with $n/2$ ones, the least expected number of rounds at a fixed tolerance $\varepsilon>0$ is $\Theta_\varepsilon((\log n)^2)$ under the first criterion but $(e^{-\varepsilon}+o(1))\log_2\ln n$ under the second, and the double-logarithmic order is attainable with the same round count on every run. For this target, a count-state recursion gives the exact least output divergence at every round cap over all causal randomized policies. The separation extends to weighted fixed-count targets with bounded weight ratios and quota fractions bounded away from zero and one, without permutation symmetry, and to the full-support Beta$(1,1)$--Bernoulli target, where the sharp expected cost under the output-law criterion is $(e^{-\varepsilon}/2+o(1))\log_2\log_2n$, attained with rare $n$-round runs. Prior work implies the order of the schedule-averaged cost on the balanced target and its $O_\varepsilon((\log n)^2)$ upper bounds on both extensions.

papers.title: Detecting Random Geometric Graphs with General Kernel
papers.abstract: We study testing a random geometric graph with a fixed kernel against an Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph with the same edge density. Under the null hypothesis, the graph has $n$ vertices and independent edges with probability $p$. Under the alternative hypothesis, latent points $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent and uniform on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, and edges are conditionally independent with probabilities $K(\langle X_i,X_j\rangle)$, where $p=\mathbb{E}[K(\langle X_1,X_2\rangle)]$. The goal is to determine a critical dimension $d_\star = d_\star(n,K)$: the total variation distance between the two graph laws tends to one for $d\ll d_\star$ and to zero for $d\gg d_\star$. For dense graphs, [BDER16] established $d_\star\asymp n^3$ for hard threshold kernels, whereas [MWX26] proved $d_\star\asymp n^{3/4}$ for smooth kernels with $K'(0)\ne0$. We connect these results by characterizing the detection thresholds for kernels that need not be differentiable at zero. We also determine the thresholds for smooth kernels whose first nonzero derivative at zero has finite order greater than one. Throughout these classes, signed triangle or quadrilateral counts attain the optimal detection threshold. For certain nondifferentiable kernels, quadrilateral counts are optimal while triangle counts are suboptimal.

papers.title: Efficient lifts into odd dimensions of Spherical $5$- and $7$-designs with Balanced Halves
papers.abstract: We propose constructions of spherical $5$- and $7$-designs in odd dimensions by lifting balanced halves of even-dimensional designs to several layers of suitable latitudes. For every odd dimension, we obtain an explicit spherical $5$-design with at most $60(d^2-1)$ points, attaining the optimal quadratic order in the dimension. Assuming Zauner's conjecture, this bound improves to $7.5(d-1)^2$. For every odd $d \geq 9$, we also construct a spherical $7$-design with $110M$ points from a complex projective $3$-design with $M$ points in $\mathbb{CP}^{(d-3)/2}$.

papers.title: Coset Lifted Product Codes: Constructing Quantum LDPC Codes from Non-Normal Subgroup Actions
papers.abstract: We introduce coset lifted product (CLP) codes, a family of quantum LDPC codes that combine the protograph structure of lifted product codes with the coset action of Aydin, Tamo, and Barg \cite{AydinTamoBarg2026}. Given a finite group $G$, a subgroup $H \le G$ that need not be normal, a protograph $A$ over $\mathbb F_2[G]$, and a protograph $B$ over $\mathbb F_2[N_G(H)]$, the two protographs act on the cosets $G/H$ from the left and from the right to produce quantum CSS codes. Further, for groups of odd order, we give an explicit formula for the dimension as a sum over the irreducible representations $\rho$ of $G$ of hypergraph product dimensions. A search over $14,843$ pairs $(G,H)$ with $H$ restricted to be non-normal and $120 \le n \le 400$ yields certified codes that exceed the best published value of $Q=kd^2/n$ at check weights $6,7$ and $9$, i.e., we obtain $[[360,20,20]]$ at $w=6$, a $[[360,24,20]]$ code at $w=7$, and codes $[[252,16,18]]$ and $[[288,16,20]]$ at $w=9$. Our search also produce high-distance codes with parameters $[[168,10,14]], [[240,8,20]]$ at $w=6$ and $[[216,8,18]]$ at $w=7$.

papers.title: A Simple Explicit Construction of Smaller Strong Blocking Sets
papers.abstract: Alon, Bishnoi, Das and Neri constructed sequences of strong blocking sets in $(k-1)$-dimension projective space $P({\bf F}_q, k-1)$ with sizes at most $Cqk$, where $k$ goes to the infinity and $C$ is a fixed positive constant not depending on $q$, in their paper published in Transactions AMS, vol. 277, pp. 5389-5410, 2024. This is equivalent to a sequence of minimal $[n_i,k_i]_q$ codes with positive rate $\frac{k_i}{n_i} \geq c$, where $k_i$ goes to the infinity and $c$ is a fixed positive constant only depending on $q$. They solved one of the main open problems on minimal codes. The Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri construction was based on asymptotically good sequences of algebraic geometric codes and expander graphs. However, the constant $C$ is large for small prime power $q$. In this paper, based on a simple approach using $(q-1)$-power intersecting algebraic geometric codes via concatenation to construct minimal codes, we construct explicit strong blocking sets in $(k-1)$-dimension projective space with sizes around $2(q^2-1)k$, equivalently, explicit minimal $[n,k]_q$ codes with length around $2(q^2-1)k$. This is an essential improvement on the previous result of Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri, when $q \leq 11$. For large $q$, strong blocking sets and minimal codes in our construction are worse than the previous construction of Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri. However, our approach is much simpler and does not depend on expander graphs.

papers.title: Certified Outage Dimensioning of Fluid Antenna Receivers: Required SNR, Aperture, and Port Count
papers.abstract: We study the SNR, aperture, and port count needed to meet a target outage in a single-user downlink with a fixed transmit antenna and a single-RF fluid antenna receiver. For known spatially correlated Rayleigh channels and ideal port selection, a sampling-free residual certificate controls reduced-rank outage error over a continuous SNR interval. Positive Bessel features support large arrays, and bounded importance sampling converts the certificate into simultaneous design intervals. At 1 bit/s/Hz and outage $10^{-5}$, a four-wavelength, ten-port receiver requires 4.40--4.55 dB. Reducing its port count from 256 to ten costs 0.70--1.25 dB under a joint 95\% probability statement. At 3.5 wavelengths, ten ports require 4.90--5.05 dB. Integer-port screening across 3--8 dB shows how aperture and port requirements change with available SNR; an effective-SNR transformation extends these decisions to other rates. The reported intervals include model and sampling uncertainty under checked Gaussian covariance inputs. A constructive slow-growth rank bound and a 16--1024-port study support compact evaluation as port count grows.

papers.title: JEPA-kMMVAE: CSI Prediction for Time-Varying Wireless Channels
papers.abstract: This paper considers channel state information (CSI) prediction using neural networks for time-varying multi-antenna channels from noisy historical observations. The main challenge is to exploit temporal correlation while distinguishing channel evolution from observation noise. We propose JEPA-kMMVAE, which combines a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a k-memory Markov variational autoencoder to predict future CSI through temporally structured latent representations. The framework supports direct prediction and residual corrections relative to the latest latent state and noisy CSI observation. Simulation results show that the residual configuration outperforms the evaluated baselines at moderate and high input CSI signal-to-noise ratios, while sequence baselines remain more accurate under stronger noise.

papers.title: Tri-Hybrid SWIPT with Reconfigurable Parasitic Antennas
papers.abstract: We propose a coupling-aware tri-hybrid precoding architecture for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) using reconfigurable parasitic antennas. By integrating multiport network theory and information theory, we develop a third precoding layer that explicitly accounts for mutual coupling and reactive energy storage within the antenna domain. To efficiently optimize this architecture, we propose a low-complexity tri-hybrid solution comprising coordinate descent (CD) for parasitic reactive load optimization, a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based analog precoder, and a protective partial zero-forcing (PPZF) digital precoder. Numerical results demonstrate that the transmit array introduces impedance mismatch that reduces the real power accepted by the antenna array. Moreover, the proposed tri-hybrid architecture significantly outperforms hybrid precoding by constructively exploiting the coupling effects, yielding substantial gains in spectral efficiency (SE) and sum non-linear harvested energy (NLHE) at a fraction of the hardware cost.

papers.title: GPU-Based Parallel BP Decoding for Quantum LDPC Memory
papers.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) decoding requires reliable corrections and low latency over long syndrome histories. We extend BP-SF, an oscillation-guided belief-propagation (BP) decoder with independent syndrome-flip trials, by introducing windowed and streaming operations. Our CUDA implementation combines disordered-memory retries, sliding windows, correlation-aware graphs, and layered scheduling. Circuit-level simulations test fixed-basis memory and complete logical Pauli-frame recovery. On the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle code at physical error rate p = 0.002, parallel BP-SF reduces 99.9th-percentile call latency by a factor of 13.15 relative to an eight-chain Relay-BP GPU baseline on 100,000 matched samples for which every tested method's initial BP stage fails within 80 iterations. Windowed BP-SF maintains a flat logical error rate and nearly constant per-round compute time through 512 rounds, reaching a 17.1-fold speedup over monolithic decoding. In 512-round full-frame streaming decoding with 2.97-ms syndrome arrivals, layered BP-SF on a transformed joint graph with 20 retries reduces 99.9th-percentile correction-release age from 166.29 to 36.25 ms relative to the joint graph with flooding updates and 100 retries. These results connect parallel BP post-processing to lower decoding costs and earlier correction release in streaming quantum memory.

papers.title: Fundamental limits for thermodynamic control with quantum feedback
papers.abstract: The study of feedback control inspired by Maxwell's demon has yielded fundamental insights into the relationship between thermodynamics and information. However, its fully quantum formulation, where the controller holds quantum side information that cannot be treated as a classical record, remains incomplete. In this paper, we establish fundamental no-go limits for thermodynamic state conversion while allowing quantum side information to be fed back to the system coherently. From two basic operational principles respected by all physically admissible feedback-control schemes, we derive the tightest possible bounds on the single-shot work of formation and extractable work for arbitrary quantum systems conditioned on arbitrary quantum side information. In the asymptotic limit, these bounds yield a generalized second law of thermodynamics with quantum feedback, governed by a conditional free energy. We further show that this generalized second law is consistent with the traditional second law once the acquisition, processing, and reset of side information are accounted for. These results extend information thermodynamics to the fully quantum regime and provide precise thermodynamic meanings for the negativity of single-shot conditional entropies.

papers.title: Coherent Information Deletion: Bayesian, Generalized Bayesian and Possibilistic Unlearning
papers.abstract: Bayes' theorem admits an information processing interpretation due to Zellner (1988): under the Shannon information criterion, the posterior is the unique rule that processes prior and data information without information loss. We revisit these ideas from the perspective of information deletion. Given a posterior based on a complete dataset, what distribution should replace it when a subset of the data is removed? For ordinary Bayesian inference, we show that the corresponding information deletion objective is uniquely minimized by the leave-data-out posterior. We then extend the framework beyond likelihood-based inference from Bayes to the generalized Bayesian updating of Bissiri et al.(2016} based on loss functions. Requiring deletion to be coherent under sequential removal of loss contributions yields a deletion rule that exactly recovers the generalized posterior based only on the retained information. We further develop an axiomatic theory, beyond probabilistic inference, for possibilistic deletion and show that the same information-deletion perspective leads to a principled rule for exact possibilistic unlearning. Finally, restricting these exact deletion principles to tractable families leads naturally to variational Bayesian, generalized Bayesian, and maxitive possibilistic unlearning.

papers.title: Locally Private Parametric Methods for Change-Point Detection
papers.abstract: We study parametric change-point detection under local differential privacy, focusing on the offline localization of a single change point in a sequence of independent observations.~In the non-private setting, we derive improved finite-sample accuracy guarantees for a generalized likelihood-ratio estimator using martingale methods.~We establish finite-sample minimax lower bounds in both the non-private and locally private settings, showing that localization accuracy is fundamentally limited by the Chernoff information between the pre- and post-change distributions.~Guided by this, we design locally private CPD algorithms based on aggregated randomized response and binary mechanisms, which maximize the Chernoff information between the induced output distributions in low- and high-privacy regimes, respectively, and derive their finite-sample guarantees. Together, our upper and lower bounds quantify the statistical cost of privacy in change-point localization.~As part of our analysis, we also show that strong data processing inequality coefficients of R\'enyi divergence and Jeffreys--R\'enyi divergence of order infinity can be computed by restricting to pairs of input distributions with a common support of at most two symbols.~We corroborate our results through empirical evaluation on synthetic data.

papers.title: From an entropic inequality for sums in abelian groups to the theorems of Ruzsa and Pl\"unnecke
papers.abstract: We give a direct information-theoretic proof of the Pl\"unnecke--Ruzsa inequalities for finite subsets of abelian groups. The argument rests on an elementary coupling inequality proved by maximizing joint entropy, without tensor powers or asymptotic constructions. It also yields Ruzsa's sumset triangle inequality and an extension to non-abelian groups.

papers.title: Linear codes over a mixed-alphabet ring and their Gray images with applications to projective and locally repairable codes
papers.abstract: Let $m \geq 2$ be an integer, and let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be the finite field of prime power order $q.$ Let $\mathcal{R}=\frac{\mathbb{F}_q[u]}{\langle u^2 \rangle}\times \mathbb{F}_q$ be the mixed-alphabet ring, where $\frac{\mathbb{F}_q[u]}{\langle u^2 \rangle}$ is the quasi-Galois ring with maximal ideal $\langle u\rangle$ of nilpotency index $2$ and residue field $\mathbb{F}_q.$ In this paper, we construct four infinite families of linear codes over the ring $\frac{\mathbb{F}_q[u]}{\langle u^2 \rangle}$ whose defining sets are certain non-empty subsets of $\mathcal{R}^m$ associated with three simplicial complexes of $\mathbb{F}_q^m,$ each possessing a single maximal element. We explicitly determine the parameters and Lee weight distributions of these codes. We also study their Gray images and identify several infinite families of few-weight codes over $\mathbb{F}_q,$ as well as an infinite family of minimal, near-Griesmer and distance-optimal codes over $\mathbb{F}_q.$ We also observe that their Gray images are self-orthogonal codes for $q=2$ or $3.$ We determine spanning matrices of these codes. Leveraging this result, we provide two constructions of infinite families of projective few-weight codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with new parameters. As an application of our newly constructed minimal codes over $\mathbb{F}_q,$ we examine the minimal access structures of Masseys secret sharing schemes based on their duals and determine the number of dictatorial participants in these schemes. Finally, we investigate the locality properties of our newly constructed projective codes and show that these codes have locality either $2$ or $3.$ As a consequence, we obtain four infinite families of $q$-ary locally repairable codes (LRCs) with locality $2,$ and two infinite families of binary LRCs with locality $3.$
